title: The Transformer Grove

features.name: the humming station
features.desc-on-touch: A transformer block painted in weathered red. The hum here is so deep you feel it in your sternum before your ears register it.

features.name: the wire arch
features.desc-on-touch: Three wires run overhead in a perfect arc. They sing when the wind picks up, four different notes in four different years.

features.name: the resonant grove
features.desc-on-touch: Eucalyptus trees grow in rows like fence posts. The bark carries the grid pattern burned into it by decades of electrical field.

features.name: the listening antenna
features.desc-on-touch: A crude speaker made of copper and prayer, still broadcasting the ambient hum northward into the rural grid.

features.name: the circuit clearing
features.desc-on-touch: An open space where the grass has been worn away by machinery. The earth itself has become conductive.

features.name: the songbook
features.desc-on-touch: A wooden cabinet weathered grey, its interior filled with field recordings on old tape. The wires have learned each other's part.

inscription: the grid has always been singing; we just never learned to listen on the same frequency

file.name: RuralPowerTransmissions_FieldRecordings_1990s.mp3
file.note: Captured hum from seventeen substations across NSW, digitised from cassette. The stations began humming in unison around 1994. Unknown why they stopped after six months.

exits.label: back down into the locked chambers
where the wires fork into the distant farmland
toward the deep reservoir where water learns the grid
